items.followUp: What are enzymes? State two characteristics of enzymes.

rubric.why: This defines the role of an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as biological catalysts.

rubric.why: Enzymes are proteins, which is a characteristic of their nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: An enzyme acts on particular substrates or reactions.
rubric.description: States that enzymes are specific in their action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzyme specificity.

rubric.why: An enzyme is not used up in the reaction it catalyses.
rubric.description: States that enzymes remain unchanged or are not consumed during reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either accepted statement.

rubric.why: Enzymes work best under particular conditions.
rubric.description: States that enzymes have an optimum temperature or pH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating either optimum condition.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific to particular substrates or reactions.
Enzymes remain unchanged and are not consumed during reactions.
Each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Give two reasons why quantitative observations are useful in a biological investigation.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations use measurements, which make results more precise or accurate.
rubric.description: States that quantitative observations provide precise or accurate results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either accepted advantage.

rubric.why: Numerical measurements can be compared or analysed statistically.
rubric.description: States that quantitative data can be compared or analysed statistically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either accepted advantage.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations use numerical measurements, making results more precise and accurate.
The measurements can be compared and analysed statistically.
